newsitem.title: MEXICO: Family and friends mourn top Mexican drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Family and friends mourn top Mexican drug lord.

text.p: A grieving family and a horde of peasant hangers-on mourned Mexico's top drug lord on Friday as officials investigated an unconfirmed report that he was murdered in his hospital bed last week by an overdose of medicine.
A local priest led a Catholic mass on Friday morning for dead cocaine king Amado Carrillo Fuentes inside the luxury northwestern Mexican ranch belonging to his mother Aurora.

As tears streamed down the faces of relatives and friends, mourners sang a song based on the parable of the lost sheep from St. Luke's Gospel. "There is more rejoicing in the heavens for one sinner who repents than for 99 just men who do not need to repent", the words ran.

Carrillo Fuentes' three sisters, clad in black and laden with gold jewellery, had sat up all night wailing at the grey metallic coffin containing the decomposing body of their brother, who died seven days ago in mysterious circumstances.

But a heavy army and police presence outside the family ranch in the farming village of Guamuchilito, about 600 miles (1,000 km) northwest of Mexico City, appeared to have kept many mobster associates away.
Several hundred chairs laid out in the grounds of the ranch for the funeral were empty and most of the mourners appeared to be family members, ranch workers or local peasants.

In Mexico City, investigators said they were checking a report that Carrillo Fuentes died after one of the men accompanying him for his plastic surgery and liposuction operation ordered nurses to slip a drug named "Dormicum" into his intravenous drip against doctors' orders.

Reforma newspaper said on Friday, quoting medical sources, that duty nurses protested as the men ordered the dose of "Dormicum" in the early hours of the morning. The report said the drug stopped his heart and breathing.
Medics treating him had explicitly forbidden any such treatment, as they did not want him given any additional medication after his surgery, it added.
"It's not possible to be sure whether they killed him or not," said Mexico's top anti-drug agent Mariano Herran Salvatti in a radio interview. "We still can't determine the cause of death."
At the Carrillo Fuentes ranch, troops and anti-drug agents searched mourners for weapons early on Friday as they left the all-night wake.
Family sources told Reuters they expected his body to be buried in front of the ranch's private grey marble chapel around midday.
A truckload of heavily armed soldiers backed by an armoured personnel carrier sat outside in the street amid rumours of plainclothes military intelligence agents infiltrating the funeral.
"They are seeing if we have got any weapons, but of course we don't," an enraged woman, who declined to give her name, told Reuters.
Friends said the durg lord's mother Aurora was furious at authorities for first delaying the handover of the body, then disrupting the wake and funeral preparations.
Although U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration officials identified the body on Sunday, Mexican authorities waited until Thursday evening to confirm Carrillo Fuentes' death.
U.S. officials considered Carrillo Fuentes the most important figure in the Mexican drug trade, shipping tonnes of cocaine a year to the United States from his base in northern Mexico.

Carrillo Fuentes, the so-called "Lord of the Skies", was head of the Juarez drug cartel and earned his nickname from the huge air shipments of Colombian cocaine he flew to Mexico and smuggled across the United States border.

At the meticulously-kept ranch where his mother held the wake, family friends allowed dozens of reporters to enter the compound at 2 a.m. (4 a.m. EDT/0800 GMT)) in a bid to prevent soldiers from storming the heavily-guarded residence.
"If it hadn't been for all the journalists, the army would have entered," Carlos Soto, a childhood friend of Carrillo Fuentes, told Reuters.
Officers and senior police commanders on the scene refused to answer reporters questions. No arrests were seen.
